Manual testing: web interface at http://localhost:8080 (Docker) or http://localhost/ (local). PHP 8.2/Apache, MySQL 8.0; env vars for DB credentials; live code volume mounts; containers web, db; ports 8080, 3306. No testing framework; test success and error paths.

Conventions: Classes PascalCase, class files exactly match class name; controllers end in Controller; models use singular entity nouns. Methods camelCase verbs; properties/variables descriptive camelCase; constants UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; DB tables/columns snake_case; views lowercase_with_underscores in subdirectories. 4 spaces, braces on declaration line, spaces after keywords, no trailing whitespace, blank lines between methods; 120-char soft limit. No strict types. Use type hints when appropriate.

Use `require_once` with `__DIR__` for absolute paths; dependencies at file tops before classes:
require_once __DIR__ . '/../config/database.php';
require_once __DIR__ . '/../models/User.php';

Always validate and sanitize user input: trim, check empty, validate email, enforce length limits; use `in_array()` to validate enum values. Use PDO::FETCH_ASSOC; enum DB values are strings. Always wrap DB operations in try-catch; PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION, catch specific exceptions when possible, throw generic model exceptions to controllers, collect validation errors for views. Never expose raw DB errors to users. Use prepared parameterized queries; never concatenate queries. Use `lastInsertId()` and `rowCount()` as appropriate.

Security: Always escape displayed user data with `htmlspecialchars()`; passwords use `password_hash()`/`password_verify()` (never md5/sha1). Start session with `session_start()`, destroy with `session_destroy()`; authenticate via `$_SESSION['user_id']`; never store passwords in session. Always use `header('Location: ...')` followed by `exit;`. CSRF protection is not currently implemented, but recommended for production.

Controllers handle HTTP requests/business orchestration: check `$_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD']`, validate before processing, use models, verify authentication before processing, redirect on success and render view on failure. Models encapsulate entity DB operations, include `user_id` in all queries for data isolation; return arrays for single/multiple records. Views include layout at top, escape all output, use controller variables directly, `??` for optional values, semantic HTML; keep business logic in controllers.

Start session at beginning of `index.php`; store user ID and username after login; check session in protected controllers; destroy on logout. Database uses singleton `Database`, UTF-8, default fetch mode ASSOC; handle connection errors gracefully.

Feature workflow: 1. Update `schema.sql` 2. Create model in `models/` 3. Create controller in `controllers/` 4. Create views in `views/` 5. Add route handling in `index.php` 6. Update `public/css/style.css` if needed.
